classification.difficultyReason: Construct an exact inequality proof by rationalising two reciprocals and explaining reversal of order for positive numbers.

content.prompt: By considering the reciprocals of the left-hand and right-hand sides, prove without a calculator that $\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}<\sqrt{5}-2$.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}}=\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{5}>\sqrt{5}+2=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}$.

Both original expressions are positive, so taking reciprocals reverses the inequality, proving $\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}<\sqrt{5}-2$.
answer.worked:
Both $\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}$ and $\sqrt{5}-2$ are positive. Rationalising their reciprocals gives
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}}&=\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{5}}{6-5}\\
\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}}&=\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{5},\\
\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}&=\frac{\sqrt{5}+2}{5-4}\\
\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}&=\sqrt{5}+2.
\end{align*}$$
Since $6>4$, we have $\sqrt{6}>2$. Hence
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}}>\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}.$$
Taking reciprocals of positive numbers reverses their order, so
$$\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}<\sqrt{5}-2.$$
